title: faster graphics and settings switching with a real progress overlay
lensAText: a sceptical game UX designer and performance engineer. Look at every frame and the timing table the builder cites, then check it yourself in ONE short Playwright script on dist/artifact.html at 390x844 (phone viewport copy, DPR 3, isMobile, hasTouch, Chrome DevTools Protocol Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate 4) and 1450x767: open the settings while driving and switch the graphics mode Low -> HD -> Ultra -> Low twice, plus every other setting that takes noticeable time; time each from the tap to a settled frame; check the overlay appears only when the work is noticeable, its bar fills from real progress (never jumps back, reaches 100 %, then goes), the game stays safe underneath, nothing flickers, breaks or leaks (heap after 10 switches), and the result looks the same as before. Judge: is switching clearly quicker, and does the loading display feel polished and honest?
brief: THE OWNER (2026-11-11 ~6 PM PT): "make it quicker to switch between graphics mode and have like a loading display with a status bar fill up in the meantime of switching between graphics, settings, etc. when a relatively decent amount of time will be needed to apply". HEAD is the live game (local/live-preview) this worktree was created from. (1) MEASURE FIRST: every setting in the main game that triggers work (the graphics mode/quality tiers, resolution or render scale, shadows, effects, view distance, traffic density, HUD style, car change in the garage, anything else you find), the time from the tap to a settled frame on the phone profile (390x844, DPR 3, CDP CPU throttle 4) and on desktop 1280x720, and WHY each slow one is slow (shader compiles, geometry or texture rebuilds, reflection cube bakes, shadow map reallocation, world or chunk rebuilds, a page reload). (2) MAKE THEM FASTER AT THE SOURCE: no full rebuild or reload where a partial update works; reuse caches; rebuild only what changed; pre-compile the other tiers' shader variants in idle time or with renderer.compileAsync (KHR_parallel_shader_compile where available); spread unavoidable heavy work across frames so the page never freezes; target at least 2x faster graphics-mode switching than the base on the phone profile, with identical visual results and no leaks (10 switches back and forth: no heap growth, no duplicated objects or listeners). (3) A LOADING OVERLAY WITH A STATUS BAR: it appears only when an apply will take noticeable time (measured or predicted over ~250 ms), says what is happening in plain words (e.g. 'Rebuilding shadows  3 of 5'), and its bar fills from REAL progress (completed stages or work units, monotonic, never a fake timer); the game is paused safely underneath (or the apply waits for a safe moment) and resumes cleanly; tapping again during an apply is handled (queued or ignored, never a broken state); accessible (aria-live status, keyboard focus kept, reduced motion: no animated shimmer); in the style guide's tokens (PROJECT_OC_STYLE_GUIDE.md), readable on a phone. Build it as a shared component so the venues' own quality switches can use it later (do NOT edit venue files in this lane: src/onfoot/**). (4) ADD a regression check: a graphics-tier switch finishes within a budget on the test machine, the overlay's progress is monotonic and reaches 100 % then hides, and 10 switches leave no heap growth. Avoid files other lanes are changing: src/preview/cockpit.ts and src/preview/wheel-sport.ts (the dashboard/wheel lane), src/game/drivers.ts and src/onfoot/** (the characters lane), and the other session's files (src/preview/hands*, src/onfoot/people/*, src/preview/car-wheel.ts, src/game/vehicle/Physics.ts, src/preview/spec.ts). Our own brands; honest labels stay. PROVE: npx tsc --noEmit; npm run build (one owner-test mark); npm test -- --only=boot,phone,modes and the new check; a BEFORE/AFTER timing table (phone profile and desktop) in the progress entry; frames of the overlay mid-switch at 390x844 and 1450x767 and of the settled result before/after (pixel-compare the settled frames) into tests/out/fast-settings/.
